newsitem.title: USA: Colorado student with Down's Syndrome can play ball.
newsitem.headline: Colorado student with Down's Syndrome can play ball.

text.p: A 20-year-old high school student with Down's Syndrome, said by authorities to be too old to play football, finally won his case Friday when authorities relented and said he can get back on the field.
Colorado's high school athletic board executive committee voted unanimously to ratify the decision of its commissioner to let Gabriel Lane play football, administrative assistant Kim Rose said.
The Greeley Central High School student sued this month in a bid to force the Colorado High School Activities Association to let him play football with the school's team, the Wildcats.

A federal judge in Denver dismissed the suit but strongly recommended the board take a more flexible approach to its rules. The group took the hint and voted to allow Commissioner Bob Ottewill to decide whether the student can play.

In the meantime, Lane has become a celebrity in Denver and even got to meet his idol, Denver Broncos quarterback John Elway. He will play Monday in a junior varsity game, said John Borman, athletic department head at the high school about 55 miles north of Denver.
"He just wanted a chance to play. He's held up very well," Borman said.
Athletes are not allowed to play football past the age of 19 to avoid a bigger youth hurting smaller players and to maintain a level playing field among all teams.

But the athletic body determined safety would not be a problem with Lane, who is 5 feet 3 inches tall and weighs 210 pounds, and that his presence on the field most likely would not make a difference to the outcome.
